audit.why: FAVOURED / 4-10 with the chart Galio on all seven rows matches packet.levelChart exactly and is consistent with a 50.07% win rate held by a champion who beats the lane and then leaves it. Full and content chart layers already agree — no chart edit needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr, winCon, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and breakdown.early all sold this as an AP matchup — 'AP assassins fund your lane', 'your MR makes AP trades a subscription'. Talon is entirely physical damage.
audit.why: enemyKit: Rake deals physical damage, Noxian Diplomacy is a crit stab, Shadow Assault deals physical damage. Telling a Galio player MR is his damage into Talon sends him to buy the wrong resistance at his first item — the spike that decides the lane.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to armour, Doran's Shield and the Rake return window; first-item spike now framed on armour and the three-stack bleed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names only Rake. It never states that Assassin's Path has no cooldown of its own — only the wall it used does — and never mentions Blade's End's three-stack bleed, which is what actually kills you after he disengages.
audit.why: enemyKit E: 'This ability has a low cooldown, but puts the used terrain on a long cooldown.' Passive: three Wound stacks then an attack causes heavy damage over time. Both are the real reasons a Galio dies with the trade apparently won.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d, enemyWin and breakdown.cooldowns now state the wall cooldown and the bleed.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT) and dosFull[2].d called Rake a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Rake is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Noxian Diplomacy 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 at 575 range, Shadow Assault 100/80/60.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written in; the invitation corrected to nine seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly calls Justice Punch a stun ('Justice Punch stun', 'Justice Punch stuns punish'). It is a knock-up.
audit.why: ownerKit E: 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters'. The distinction matters because tenacity reduces stun duration and does not reduce a knock-up.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[0].text, wants.you[0] and `early` now say knock-up.

edits.before: AP assassins picked the wrong statue — taunt the dive, shield the burst, and watch the assassination become community service.
edits.after: An AD assassin picked the wrong statue — taunt the leap, shield the burst, and watch the assassination become community service.

edits.before: Taunt the dive and let the shield do the arguing — AP assassins fund your lane. Rake is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Taunt the leap and let Shield of Durand do the arguing — armour, not MR, pays here. Rake is the clock this lane runs on: 9s at rank 1, read it before you step.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Talon wins by W-Q-auto into three Blade's End stacks, then vaulting a wall with Assassin's Path before you can taunt.

edits.before: Full kit: E-dash into W-taunt is the lane's rudest counter-engage. Magic damage starts paying your shield.
edits.after: Full kit: E-dash into W-taunt is the lane's rudest counter-engage, and his Q leap walks straight into it.

edits.before: Trade into AP freely — your passive shield refunds their poke and your taunt taxes their commits.
edits.after: Rake at rank 4 is 7.5s — trade on its return, and your taunt taxes every leap he answers with.

edits.before: First item spike: the full taunt rotation chunks and your MR makes AP trades a subscription you sell.
edits.after: First item: armour plus the full taunt rotation means his three-stack bleed no longer threatens a kill.

edits.before: Shield-trade the contacts and taunt the over-steps — your lane is a toll booth for magic damage.
edits.after: Talon is physical damage — Doran's Shield and armour, not MR, are what refund this lane's chip.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. It governs your forward steps. - W Shield of Durand spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1 and 7s maxed — the returning blades carry most of his lane damage, so stand off the return line and step up in that window. - Noxian Diplomacy is 8s and leaps from 575; Assassin's Path has no cooldown, only the wall does.

edits.before: If Talon gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Rake extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through taunt peel and R arrivals.
edits.after: If Talon gets a kill, the lane gets honest — buy armour and give Rake's return extra room. Two kills: stop duelling your tilt, farm with Winds of War and stay relevant through taunt peel and R arrivals.

edits.before: Carry through arrivals — Hero's Entrance turns every losing skirmish your team starts into a 5v4 with a knockup.
edits.after: Carry by peeling the reveal — Hero's Entrance knocks up the moment Shadow Assault's blades converge back on him.

edits.before: Ahead, tax both maps: zone Talon with taunt threat, keep the wave middle, and R every skirmish — fed Galio makes the enemy jungler unemployed.
edits.after: Ahead, take his walls: shove the wave, ward the raptor and river vaults, and R the side lane before Assassin's Path can get him there.

edits.before: Q the contact, let the tornado tick, E-auto if he answers, W-taunt the commit — a full rotation where his half landed on a shield.
edits.after: Assassin's Path has no cooldown but the wall he vaults does — Winds of War on the landing side catches him with no second hop.

edits.before: Talon burns Rake on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Talon burns Rake on nothing — take the nine-second invitation.

edits.before: That is Talon’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: He feints the Q leap at 575 and vaults out instead — release the taunt on contact.

edits.before: Your R locks you in place mid-channel — casting it without the wave parked is donating two waves and a tower.
edits.after: Three Blade's End stacks bleed for heavy damage over time — at even HP that bleed finishes you after he leaves.

edits.before: Charging W through a minion line at a mage holding his answer — the statue mid-charge is the lane's easiest skillshot target.
edits.after: Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1; leave without it and Assassin's Path puts him on you through a wall you cannot answer.

edits.before: You're ahead from level 1 — Talon's Rake-based poke and dive combo doesn't out-damage your own trades, and Justice Punch stuns punish any dash-in attempt cleanly. Levels 3-5 extend this further: your full combo out-trades his burst before he's itemized, so he's mostly looking to roam onto weaker lanes rather than contest you directly.
edits.after: You're ahead from level 1 — Talon's Rake-based poke and dive combo doesn't out-damage your own trades, and Justice Punch knocks him up out of any leap-in cleanly. Levels 3-5 extend this further: your full combo out-trades his burst before he's itemized, so he's mostly looking to roam onto weaker lanes rather than contest you directly.
